items.title: The Daily Meditation
items.question: Marcus meditated each morning on mortality — not morbidly, but to sharpen what the day is for. What subject focuses priorities like nothing else?
items.correctExplanation: Death — memento mori converts abstract time into today's agenda. Mortality meditated clarifies; mortality ignored merely waits.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is death. Daily remembrance of mortality isn't gloom but lenscraft: ends in view order means correctly. Priorities sharpen against finality like nothing else.
items.lessonContent:
Ends in view order daily means correctly.
Mortality meditated clarifies; ignored merely waits.
Finality is the sharpest priority filter known.
Meditate endings to begin days well.
Share this: plan one day as if numbered.

items.title: The Rehearsed Disaster
items.question: Stoics rehearsed poverty, exile, and loss in advance — not to worry, but to rob future blows of surprise. What is this exercise called?
items.correctExplanation: Premeditatio malorum — premeditation of evils. Rehearsed blows land on braced minds; surprise, not pain, does the worst damage.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is premeditatio malorum. Imagined exile inoculates against real exile's shock: the event arrives pre-discounted. Worry ruminates; rehearsal prepares — opposite uses of one faculty.
items.lessonContent:
Surprise wounds worse than events themselves.
Rehearsal inoculates where rumination infects.
Braced minds absorb unbraced ones shatter.
Pre-discount blows before fate delivers.
Share this: rehearse one feared loss tonight.

items.title: The Bread Days
items.question: Seneca advised the rich to live on bread and water for set days — rehearsing ruin while comfortable. What condition should prosperity periodically practice?
items.correctExplanation: Poverty — rehearsed ruin loses its terror: proving survival on little disarms fortune's threats. Practice makes needlessness.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is poverty. Set days of bread-and-water convert abstract fear into tested capacity: I have lived on little and lived. Rehearsal robs ruin of novelty.
items.lessonContent:
Rehearsed ruin loses its terror completely.
Bread-and-water days disarm fortune's threats.
Tested capacity beats imagined fragility.
Practice needlessness while comfortable.
Share this: live one bread day soon.

items.title: The Borderless Name
items.question: Asked what city he came from, Diogenes answered with a citizenship no map recognizes. What one word names belonging everywhere?
items.correctExplanation: Cosmopolitan — citizen of the world, local nowhere, at home anywhere reason reaches. Maps divide; membership transcends.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is cosmopolitan. Diogenes refused Sinope for the cosmos: belonging expanded past walls. Local loyalties shrink souls to postal codes.
items.lessonContent:
Belonging can exceed every map drawn.
Local loyalties shrink souls to postal codes.
Reason's reach defines true citizenship.
Walls divide what membership transcends.
Share this: claim one wider citizenship today.

items.title: The Drawn Circles
items.question: Hierocles drew rings — self, family, city, humanity — urging us to pull the outer rings inward. What must expand outward until none are strangers?
items.correctExplanation: Moral concern — drawn inward ring by ring until humanity sits in the family circle. Expansion, not contraction, is the exercise.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is moral concern. Hierocles' geometry moves strangers toward self: call humanity kin until the word means something. Circles drawn define souls' sizes.
items.lessonContent:
Strangers move inward by deliberate drawing.
Kinship expands; it never merely is.
Circle sizes measure soul sizes exactly.
Draw humanity into the family ring.
Share this: pull one outer ring inward.

items.title: The Woven Whole
items.question: Stoic physics held all things mutually intertwined — no event isolated, no soul separate. What doctrine names this interdependence?
items.correctExplanation: Sympatheia — the cosmos as one intergrown organism, every part feeling all. Isolation is the illusion; sympathy the physics.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is sympatheia. Stoic cosmology wove fate from total interconnection: touch one thread, the whole web answers. Separation is perspective, never fact.
items.lessonContent:
Isolation is perspective, never fact.
Webs answer every touch everywhere.
Interconnection precedes individuality deeply.
Sympathy here is physics, not sentiment.
Share this: tug one thread and watch the web.

items.title: The Cosmic Survey
items.question: Marcus advised viewing life from above — armies as ants, empires as garden plots — to shrink present troubles. What exercise miniaturizes worry?
items.correctExplanation: View from above — altitude dissolves urgency: troubles shrink to specks honestly. Perspective is proportion restored.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is view from above. Armies-as-ants reframes without denying: troubles stay real, sizes correct. Altitude is honesty's elevator.
items.lessonContent:
Altitude restores honest proportions fast.
Ants-armies reframe without denying facts.
Troubles shrink; duties stay sized.
Perspective is proportion, not escape.
Share this: survey one worry from orbit.

items.title: The Turned Block
items.question: 'The impediment to action advances action. What stands in the way becomes...' Complete Marcus's formula: the obstacle becomes what?
items.correctExplanation: The way — obstruction converted to material: fire feeds on barriers. Blocks become building supplies under this alchemy.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is the way. Marcus's formula transmutes hindrance into path: what blocks the road becomes the road. Alchemy, not optimism — material reuse, not wishful thinking.
items.lessonContent:
Hindrances transmute into paths deliberately.
Fire feeds on exactly what blocks it.
Blocks become supplies under right alchemy.
Reuse beats removal for obstacles.
Share this: pave with one block today.

items.title: The Frontier Tongue
items.question: A Roman emperor journals philosophy at the frontier — but not in Latin, the tongue of command. In what language did Marcus write the Meditations?
items.correctExplanation: Greek — philosophy's working tongue, even for emperors: Marcus thought in the language of Epictetus, not of legions. Command spoke Latin; reflection spoke otherwise.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is Greek. Rome ruled in Latin but reasoned in the tongue of Athens: the Meditations' Koine proves philosophy kept its first language. Empires borrow minds along with maps.
items.lessonContent:
Empires borrow minds along with maps.
Command tongues differ from reflection tongues.
Philosophy kept its first language deliberately.
Think in the tongue that thinks best.
Share this: learn one thought in translation.

items.title: The Squandered Fortune
items.question: Seneca argued we mistake our greatest wealth for free and spend it carelessly. What treasure do we waste while defending pennies?
items.correctExplanation: Time — the one treasure misers of money scatter freely. Fortunes guarded, lifetimes spilled: inverted thrift.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is time. Pennies counted, years poured out: Seneca's audit finds millionaires of moments living as beggars of attention. Thrift misapplied bankrupts truly.
items.lessonContent:
Moments misspent bankrupt millionaires of time.
Attention is the currency actually spent.
Pennies guarded, lifetimes spilled: audit this.
Thrift belongs to hours first.
Share this: budget one hour like money.

items.title: The Brief Madness
items.question: Seneca devoted a whole treatise against one passion, defining it as temporary insanity that punishes its holder first. Which passion?
items.correctExplanation: Anger — brief madness that burns its bearer before its target. Treatises exist because the passion feels like justice.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is anger. Seneca's De Ira anatomizes rage as insanity with a motive: it punishes the holder while aiming at others. Justice-feeling camouflages self-harm.
items.lessonContent:
Rage punishes holders before targets always.
Justice-feeling camouflages self-harm well.
Treatises exist where passions pose as virtues.
Brief madness needs long study.
Share this: study one flare-up coldly.

items.title: The Owned Territory
items.question: Epictetus divided existence into what is up to us and what is not. Within our power alone fall opinions, impulses, desires — broadly, what?
items.correctExplanation: Our judgments — the inner citadel no tyrant enters. Bodies chained, reputations weathered, assent free: territory mapped, freedom founded.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is our judgments. Opinions, impulses, desires, aversions: the short list of the ownable. Everything else is on loan from fortune — manage it, never mistake it for yours.
items.lessonContent:
Ownable lists are short; loan lists long.
Assent alone needs no one's permission.
Citadels stand where tyrants can't enter.
Map territory before claiming freedom.
Share this: own one judgment fully today.

items.title: The Twin Command
items.question: Marcus commanded: if an act is not right, do not do it; if a statement is not true, do not say it. What two domains does the rule govern?
items.correctExplanation: Deeds and words — rightness gates action, truth gates speech. Two filters catch every failure mode.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is deeds and words. Action filtered by right, speech filtered by true: the complete ethics of output. Inputs may enslaved be; outputs stay owned.
items.lessonContent:
Rightness gates action; truth gates speech.
Two filters catch all failure modes.
Outputs stay owned whatever inputs enslave.
Filter everything leaving you.
Share this: gate one deed and one word.

items.title: The Soul's Dye
items.question: 'The soul becomes dyed with the color of its thoughts.' What stains the inner life with its own hue?
items.correctExplanation: Thoughts — attention is immersion: minds take the tint of their dwellings. Dwell nobly, dye nobly.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is thoughts. Dye works by soaking: whatever thinking steeps in colors it permanently. Curation of mind is curation of soul by another name.
items.lessonContent:
Attention immerses; immersion tints permanently.
Dwellings dye their inhabitants surely.
Curation of mind is curation of soul.
Steep nobly to stain nobly.
Share this: notice one dye in progress.

items.title: The Ended Debate
items.question: 'Waste no more time arguing what a good man should be. Be one.' What replaces philosophical debate about virtue?
items.correctExplanation: Being good — enactment ends discussion by outperforming it. Seminars about swimming never get wet.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is being good. Debate refines maps; only walking covers ground. Marcus closes the seminar and opens the street: embodiment is the final argument.
items.lessonContent:
Walking covers ground maps only describe.
Enactment outperforms discussion always.
Seminars never get wet swimming.
Close debates by opening streets.
Share this: be one good thing today.

items.title: The Final Performance
items.question: Marcus urged living each act as if it were the last — with gravity, love, and justice. In what spirit should every deed be done?
items.correctExplanation: The last act — finality concentrates care: no rehearsals, no deferrals. Lastness dignifies trivia into ceremony.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is the last act. Treating deeds as final strips procrastination's excuse: gravity, love, justice — none survive postponement. Ceremony is attention, not occasion.
items.lessonContent:
Finality concentrates care completely.
Rehearsals end where lastness begins.
Trivia dignified becomes ceremony.
Attention, not occasion, hallows deeds.
Share this: perform one last act today.

items.title: The Morning Forecast
items.question: Marcus began days by predicting rudeness, ingratitude, and obstruction from everyone met. Whom should you expect to encounter?
items.correctExplanation: Difficult people — forecast friction, meet humans. Expectation defuses; surprise detonates.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is difficult people. Morning forecasts of busybodies and ingrates convert ambushes into appointments. Predicted weather never ruins outings.
items.lessonContent:
Forecasts convert ambushes to appointments.
Predicted friction never detonates.
Expect humans, meet them unsurprised.
Morning realism buys daily serenity.
Share this: forecast one busybody kindly.

items.title: The Unblocked Virtue
items.question: 'Does what happened keep you from acting with justice, generosity, and truth? Then nothing blocks the good.' What must events never obstruct?
items.correctExplanation: Virtuous action — externals touch circumstances, never character's output. Justice needs no permission from events.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is virtuous action. Happening cannot cancel character: generosity needs no favorable weather. Outputs stay sovereign whatever inputs suffer.
items.lessonContent:
Character outputs need no weather permission.
Events touch settings, never virtues.
Justice operates in all climates.
Sovereignty lives in responses, not scenes.
Share this: act justly in bad weather.

items.title: The Judgment Layer
items.question: 'The universe is change; our life is what our thoughts make it.' In this formula, what is a human life?
items.correctExplanation: Opinion — life equals the mind's take, not the world's give. Change the take, change the life: idealism with work boots.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is opinion. Flux outside, verdict inside: living happens at the judgment layer. Takes can be retaken — that is the entire freedom.
items.lessonContent:
Living happens at the judgment layer.
Takes retaken remake lives entirely.
Flux outside, verdict inside, always.
Idealism wears work boots here.
Share this: retake one verdict today.

items.title: The Pain's Author
items.question: 'If you are distressed by anything external, the pain is due to your estimate of it.' According to Marcus, what authors the distress?
items.correctExplanation: Your estimate — externals propose, judgments dispose. Pain's authorship sits inside, whatever the occasion.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is your estimate. Events deliver raw material; valuations manufacture distress. Authorship implies editorship: re-estimate to relieve.
items.lessonContent:
Valuations manufacture all distress suffered.
Raw material differs from finished pain.
Authorship implies editorship always.
Re-estimate to relieve genuinely.
Share this: re-estimate one distress today.

items.title: The Worthy Bar
items.question: Seneca warned that fearing death guarantees a specific failure: never doing anything worthy of a living person. What does death-fear prevent?
items.correctExplanation: Worthy action — the fearful survive without living: breathing biographies, empty resumes. Boldness needs mortality faced.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is worthy action. Death-fear purchases safety at life's price: unrisked years sum to unlived ones. Worthiness demands the wager fear refuses.
items.lessonContent:
Unrisked years sum to unlived ones.
Safety purchased costs life itself.
Worthiness demands wagers fear refuses.
Breathe biographies, or write them.
Share this: wager once worthily today.

items.title: The Ample Years
items.question: Seneca insisted life is not short but squandered — ample if well spent. Properly used, what is life's true length?
items.correctExplanation: Life — length suffices; spending fails. Complaints about brevity confess prodigality.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is life. 'Short life' indicts the liver, never the lifespan: ample years poured down trivial drains. Audit spending before mourning supply.
items.lessonContent:
Brevity complaints confess prodigality.
Supply suffices; spending fails reliably.
Audit outflows before mourning inflows.
Ample years await competent livers.
Share this: spend one hour un-squandered.

items.title: The Lucky Meeting
items.question: Seneca defined luck as the crossroads of two forces. When opportunity arrives, what must already be waiting?
items.correctExplanation: Preparation — opportunity knocks for ready ears only. Luck favors the rehearsed, never the idle.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is preparation. Crossroads need both roads: chance arrives unbidden, readiness is built. Unprepared meetings are accidents, not luck.
items.lessonContent:
Crossroads need both roads traveled.
Readiness converts accidents into luck.
Chance arrives; preparation receives.
Build before opportunity knocks.
Share this: prepare one unpromised meeting.

items.title: The Inner Master
items.question: 'No man is free who is not master of himself.' Epictetus makes freedom conditional on ruling what territory?
items.correctExplanation: Oneself — self-mastery precedes all liberties: the unruled within obey every without. Kingdoms start at home or nowhere.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is oneself. External freedoms decorate internal servitude meaninglessly: appetites unruled make citizens of impulse. Rule within or be ruled without.
items.lessonContent:
Internal servitude voids external freedoms.
Appetites unruled make impulse citizens.
Kingdoms start at home or nowhere.
Rule within first, always.
Share this: master one impulse today.

items.title: The Revealing Storm
items.question: Epictetus taught that circumstances don't make a person but expose them. What do hard times do to character?
items.correctExplanation: Reveal character — storms display seams, never sew them. Pressure publishes what comfort drafts.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is reveal character. Making implies creation; exposing implies prior existence. Blame the mirror, never the storm, for the face shown.
items.lessonContent:
Storms publish what comfort drafts.
Pressure displays seams, never sews.
Mirrors blamed wrongly for faces shown.
Existence precedes exposure always.
Share this: read one storm's revelation.
